cards.explanation: The answer is showing hospitality to strangers. The writer says that by doing it, “…some people have entertained angels without knowing it.” That's why I'd wipe down every counter in my bakery for any stranger who walks in. Nobody gets the crumby table, friends. (Hebrews 13:2)

The answer is as if you were bound with them. The line is “Remember those in prison as if you were bound with them…” He doesn't say to remember them from a distance. I think he means to feel it like it's happening to you. And he adds the mistreated too, “…as if you were suffering with them.” (Hebrews 13:3)

The answer is False. The writer says, “Marriage should be honored by all and the marriage bed kept undefiled…” He doesn't limit it to the married. He adds that God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterers. (Hebrews 13:4)

The answer is that God has said He will never leave them. The writer says to be content with what you have, for God has said, “Never will I leave you, never will I forsake you.” The cookie jar may run low, friends, but that promise doesn't. Having God with you is a lot of treasure. (Hebrews 13:5)

The answer is True. Right after the promise, the writer says we say with confidence, “The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?” The confidence comes from God staying close. And that question at the end makes me stand up a little taller. (Hebrews 13:5–6)

The answer is imitate. The writer says to remember your leaders who spoke the word of God to you, consider the outcome of their way of life, and “…imitate their faith.” Notice what he points to: their faith. That's the part to copy, friends. (Hebrews 13:7)

The answer is teachings. The writer says, “Do not be carried away by all kinds of strange teachings…” Carried away sounds like getting swept off by a current to me. He wants their hearts to stay put. (Hebrews 13:9)

The answer is grace. The writer says, “…it is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace and not by foods of no value to those devoted to them.” The foods didn't do those folks any good. Grace is what holds the heart up. (Hebrews 13:9)

The answer is outside the city gate. The writer says, “And so Jesus also suffered outside the city gate, to sanctify the people by His own blood.” That matches the animal bodies burned outside the camp in the verse before. He's connecting the two. (Hebrews 13:11–12)

The answer is the disgrace He bore. The writer says, “Therefore let us go to Him outside the camp, bearing the disgrace He bore.” It's not a comfortable invitation. But it's an invitation to go to Jesus. (Hebrews 13:13)

The answer is False. The writer says, “For here we do not have a permanent city, but we are looking for the city that is to come.” So no permanent city here, but one is coming. That's a good thing to know when the moving boxes pile up. (Hebrews 13:14)

The answer is praise. The writer says, “Through Jesus, therefore, let us continually offer to God a sacrifice of praise, the fruit of lips that confess His name.” Lips that confess His name are what make the fruit. Nothing to carry, nothing to count. (Hebrews 13:15)

The answer is doing good and sharing with others. The writer says, “And do not neglect to do good and to share with others, for with such sacrifices God is pleased.” So doing good and sharing both count as sacrifices. I'll hand out a few extra cookies today, friends. (Hebrews 13:16)
The answer is give an account. The writer says leaders “…watch over your souls as those who must give an account.” That's a serious job. I'd say they deserve our patience, friends. (Hebrews 13:17)

The answer is True. The writer says, “…allow them to lead with joy and not with grief, for that would be of no advantage to you.” So grief doesn't help the people. A joyful leader is a gift to everybody. (Hebrews 13:17)

The answer is that he may be restored to them soon. The writer says, “And I especially urge you to pray that I may be restored to you soon.” The word especially tells me this one matters to him. I think he misses them. (Hebrews 13:19)

The answer is the blood of the eternal covenant. The writer says God “…through the blood of the eternal covenant brought back from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great Shepherd of the sheep…” That's a big line to pack into one sentence. It's worth reading twice. (Hebrews 13:20)
The answer is will. The writer says, “…equip you with every good thing to do His will.” God does the equipping, and we get to do the doing. That takes a lot of pressure off, friends. (Hebrews 13:21)

The answer is False. The writer says, “I urge you, brothers, to bear with my word of exhortation, for I have only written to you briefly.” He says he wrote briefly, not at length. So he's asking them to bear with it. (Hebrews 13:22)

The answer is that Timothy has been released. The writer says, “Be aware that our brother Timothy has been released.” Then he adds that if Timothy arrives soon, he will come with him to see them. So the news about Timothy comes with a possible visit. (Hebrews 13:23)

The answer is True. The writer says, “If he arrives soon, I will come with him to see you.” The plan hangs on that if, friends: Timothy has to arrive soon. I think it's a warm way to end a letter. (Hebrews 13:23)
